Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[4].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[4].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.
Enum.name: NOT_VALID

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

BitField.description: Indicates whether the channel's control structure will be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted. Reloading allows ping-pong and linked transfers.

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[7].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[7].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.
BitField.name: CFGVALID

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.
Enum.name: NOT_VALID

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.
Enum.name: VALID

BitField.description: Indicates whether the channel's control structure will be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted. Reloading allows ping-pong and linked transfers.

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[10].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[10].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

BitField.description: Indicates whether the channel's control structure will be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted. Reloading allows ping-pong and linked transfers.

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[13].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[13].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

BitField.description: Indicates whether the channel's control structure will be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted. Reloading allows ping-pong and linked transfers.

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[16].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[16].XFERCFG

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[19].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[19].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[22].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[22].XFERCFG

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.

Enum.description: Not cleared. The trigger is not cleared when this descriptor is exhausted. If there is a reload, the next descriptor will be started.
Enum.name: NOT_CLEARED

Enum.description: Cleared. The trigger is cleared when this descriptor is exhausted
Enum.name: CLEARED

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag A for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTA

Enum.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Set Interrupt flag B for this channel. There is no hardware distinction between interrupt A and B. They can be used by software to assist with more complex descriptor usage. By convention, interrupt A may be used when only one interrupt flag is needed.
BitField.name: SETINTB

Enum.description: Set. The INTB flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: SET

BitField.description: Transfer width used for this DMA channel.
BitField.name: WIDTH

Enum.description: 8-bit. 8-bit transfers are performed (8-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_8

Enum.description: 16-bit. 6-bit transfers are performed (16-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_16

Enum.description: 32-bit. 32-bit transfers are performed (32-bit source reads and destination writes).
Enum.name: BIT_32

BitField.description: Determines whether the source address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: SRCINC

Enum.description: No increment. The source address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The source address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the source is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The source address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The source address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Determines whether the destination address is incremented for each DMA transfer.
BitField.name: DSTINC

Enum.description: No increment. The destination address is not incremented for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is a peripheral device.
Enum.name: NO_INCREMENT

Enum.description: 1 x width. The destination address is incremented by the amount specified by Width for each transfer. This is the usual case when the destination is memory.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_1

Enum.description: 2 x width. The destination address is incremented by 2 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_2

Enum.description: 4 x width. The destination address is incremented by 4 times the amount specified by Width for each transfer.
Enum.name: WIDTH_X_4

BitField.description: Total number of transfers to be performed, minus 1 encoded. The number of bytes transferred is: (XFERCOUNT + 1) x data width (as defined by the WIDTH field). The DMA controller uses this bit field during transfer to count down. Hence, it cannot be used by software to read back the size of the transfer, for instance, in an interrupt handler. 0x0 = a total of 1 transfer will be performed. 0x1 = a total of 2 transfers will be performed. 0x3FF = a total of 1,024 transfers will be performed.
BitField.name: XFERCOUNT

BitField.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.
BitField.name: PERIPHREQEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.
BitField.name: HWTRIGEN

Enum.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.
Enum.name: DISABLED

BitField.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.
BitField.name: TRIGPOL

Enum.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING

Enum.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.
Enum.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING

BitField.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.
BitField.name: TRIGTYPE

Enum.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.
Enum.name: EDGE

Enum.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.
Enum.name: LEVEL

BitField.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.
BitField.name: TRIGBURST

Enum.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.
Enum.name: SINGLE

Enum.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.
Enum.name: BURST

BitField.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register). When the TRIGBURST field elsewhere in this register = 1, Burst Power selects how many transfers are performed for each DMA trigger. This can be used, for example, with peripherals that contain a FIFO that can initiate a DMA operation when the FIFO reaches a certain level. 0000: Burst size = 1 (20). 0001: Burst size = 2 (21). 0010: Burst size = 4 (22). 1010: Burst size = 1024 (210). This corresponds to the maximum supported transfer count. others: not supported. The total transfer length as defined in the XFERCOUNT bits in the XFERCFG register must be an even multiple of the burst size.
BitField.name: BURSTPOWER

BitField.description: Source Burst Wrap. When enabled, the source data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the source address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to read several sequential registers from a peripheral for each DMA burst, reading the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: SRCBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Source burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Source burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Destination Burst Wrap. When enabled, the destination data address for the DMA is 'wrapped', meaning that the destination address range for each burst will be the same. As an example, this could be used to write several sequential registers to a peripheral for each DMA burst, writing the same registers again for each burst.
BitField.name: DSTBURSTWRAP

Enum.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.
Enum.name: ENABLED

BitField.description: Priority of this channel when multiple DMA requests are pending. Eight priority levels are supported: 0x0 = highest priority. 0x7 = lowest priority.
BitField.name: CHPRIORITY

Register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[25].CTLSTAT

BitField.description: Valid pending flag for this channel. This bit is set when a 1 is written to the corresponding bit in the related SETVALID register when CFGVALID = 1 for the same channel.
BitField.name: VALIDPENDING

Enum.description: No effect. No effect on DMA operation.
Enum.name: NO_EFFECT

BitField.description: Trigger flag. Indicates that the trigger for this channel is currently set. This bit is cleared at the end of an entire transfer or upon reload when CLRTRIG = 1.
BitField.name: TRIG

Enum.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.
Enum.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

Enum.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.
Enum.name: TRIGGERED

Register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel .
Register.name: CHANNEL[25].XFERCFG

BitField.description: Configuration Valid flag. This bit indicates whether the current channel descriptor is valid and can potentially be acted upon, if all other activation criteria are fulfilled.
BitField.name: CFGVALID

Enum.description: Not valid. The channel descriptor is not considered valid until validated by an associated SETVALID0 setting.
Enum.name: NOT_VALID

Enum.description: Valid. The current channel descriptor is considered valid.
Enum.name: VALID

BitField.description: Indicates whether the channel's control structure will be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted. Reloading allows ping-pong and linked transfers.
BitField.name: RELOAD

Enum.description: Enabled. Reload the channels' control structure when the current descriptor is exhausted.
Enum.name: ENABLED
